description.purpose: The night watchdog of the keeper (R-AG-1, GH #1229). It carries no schedule of its own: ./close keeps one one-shot named `night-close` under a fixed id and re-arms it (`rearm`) -- for the next opening of the night window when a generation opens by day, and after every firing for the moment the generation that falls silent next crosses the idle threshold. It sends, it does not decide -- schedule_name is what the close pass recognises as a firing.
description.use_when: Inside the session-keeper hive, always. It is not a poll: a keeper with no open generation orders nothing and the timer stays silent all night. The window is a pair of knobs of ./close, `night_from_utc` and `night_until_utc`.
description.not_in_scope: No cron: the former thirty-minute night cron is gone, and with it the twelve strikes a night that asked the store even when nothing was open. A strike missed while the colony was down fires once on the next start (`catch_up`, marked `late`); outside the night ./close seals nothing on it and arms the next night. No judgement about sessions; the timer knows nothing about channels.
description.emits_meaning: hop.schedule_name = 'night-close' is the marker the hive edge carries to the close pass, and hop.late = true marks a strike that fired after a stop. The body is a plain trigger. A refused order leaves as `timer_op_error`.
description.consumes_meaning: Schedule ops (add/modify/remove/trigger by schedule_id) as body.op -- in practice the one `add` with `at`, `rearm` and `catch_up` that ./close sends on route 'night'.
examples: a generation opens at 14:00 UTC -> ./close orders one strike for 22:00 UTC = 00:00 CEST
the strike at 22:00 UTC -> the close pass sweeps and orders the next strike for the moment the next open generation turns two hours silent, or none
